newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says case of 1996 July riots 'closed'.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says case of 1996 July riots 'closed'.

text.p: Indonesian Coordinating Minister for Politics and Security Susilo Sudarman said on Thursday the government regarded the case of the riots in the capital Jakarta in July last year as being closed.

The official National Commission of Human Rights in a report in October last year found five people had died, 23 were missing and 149 injured in the disturbance in which scores of vehicles and buildings were burnt in the worst rioting in Jakarta in 20 years.
"The problems (are) already past, as for the problems of the missing people, efforts have already been made to find them, so it's over," Sudarman told reporters after a monthly security meeting.
"Who says it's not finished? The government has already answered the human rights commission recommendations," he said.
Human rights commission sources said the government's response in May blamed the riots on the internal problems of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
However, the commission in its report criticised security forces for excessive interference in the political process.

Hundreds of supporters of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri peacefully took to the streets of Jakarta on Sunday to mark the first anniversary of the riots. More than 80 supporters were detained for holding an illegal gathering as police had banned the gathering, but were later released.
The 1996 riots were sparked by a police-backed raid on PDI headquarters after Megawati supporters refused to vacate the building despite her ouster by a government-backed rival.
